$comment: CrossScore: route-condition model. Read by packages/engine/src/crossscore.ts. Changing any number requires a version bump and a CHANGELOG entry in docs/METHODOLOGY.md.
name: CrossScore
summary: CrossScore (0-100) summarizes the transportation conditions along a route from public crash, road and infrastructure data. Higher means fewer risk indicators were found. It is not a prediction and not a promise of personal safety.

factors.label: Crash history
factors.description: Reported crashes within 30 m of the route, compared with the average for Georgia roads in the same setting (from quiet areas to dense urban cores, or interstates and freeways).

factors.label: Injury and fatal crashes
factors.description: Crashes with a reported injury or death within 30 m of the route, compared with the average for Georgia roads in the same setting.

factors.label: Pedestrian incidents
factors.description: Crashes involving a pedestrian within 30 m of the route, compared with the average for Georgia streets in the same setting.

factors.label: Bicycle incidents
factors.description: Crashes involving a bicyclist within 30 m of the route, compared with the average for Georgia streets in the same setting.

factors.label: Road speed
factors.description: Distance-weighted posted speed limit on the streets the route uses, converted with the pedestrian impact-speed risk curve (Tefft 2011). Only used where at least 30% of street distance has a recorded limit.

factors.label: Number of lanes
factors.description: Share of the route on or alongside roads with 3 or more through lanes. Wider roads mean longer crossings and more conflict points (FHWA STEP guide, 2018).

factors.label: Traffic volume
factors.description: Daily traffic on the major roads the route uses, scored with the FHWA STEP volume thresholds (9,000 / 12,000 / 15,000 vehicles per day). Local streets are not counted by GDOT and are treated as below 9,000.

factors.label: Sidewalk availability
factors.description: Share of the walk on footpaths, or on streets where OpenStreetMap records a sidewalk. A street without a recorded sidewalk may still have one, so this is a lower bound.

factors.label: Protected path availability
factors.description: Share of the ride on separated paths or protected lanes (full credit), painted bike lanes (60%) or shared-lane markings (30%).

factors.label: Crossing exposure
factors.source: GDOT Road Inventory 2025 and GDOT traffic signals
factors.description: How many times the route crosses an arterial or a road with 4+ lanes, and whether a GDOT traffic signal is recorded at the crossing.

crashScale.$comment: Crash factors compare the crashes found along a route with the average for Georgia roads in the same setting (crashes per km x length). score = 100 / (1 + ratio x (100 - averageScore) / averageScore): no crashes = 100, exactly average = 70, twice average = 54, four times = 37.

speedRisk.$comment: Pedestrian risk of death by impact speed, Tefft (2011), AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety: 10% at 23 mph, 25% at 32 mph, 50% at 42 mph, 75% at 50 mph, 90% at 58 mph. Score = 100 x (1 - risk), linear between points.
speedRisk.reference: Tefft, B.C. (2011). Impact Speed and a Pedestrian's Risk of Severe Injury or Death. AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety.

laneScores.$comment: Score per meter by through lanes; roads not in the GDOT major-road index are local streets with 1-2 lanes.

selection.$comment: How the safest, balanced and fastest routes are chosen from the alternatives.

curb.$comment: Safer pickup and drop-off: curb points within a short walk are compared on the conditions right at the curb.

confidence.$comment: Share of the mode's total factor weight that had usable data.
